phase_0.boundary_condition: The completed diamond cubic crystal lattice with its surface termination closes and contains the system.

⊢.justification: The uninitialized state before any germanium atoms arrange into a crystal lattice.

⊣.justification: The fully formed diamond cubic structure with surface termination acts as the closed boundary containing the entire system.

≻.justification: Forward morphism representing the directional growth of the crystal lattice through successive bond formation.

≺.justification: Reverse morphism representing the descent into disorder when thermal energy overcomes the kinetic barrier.

⋈.justification: Sequential chaining of tetrahedral units into the extended network through covalent bond composition.

⊙.justification: The crystal structure recognizes its own periodicity and symmetry through Bragg diffraction and phonon modes.

∈.justification: The growth front splits into a perfect tetrahedral coordination branch and a defective coordination branch.

∋.justification: The lattice rejoins the perfect and defective arms by incorporating point defects into the overall structure.

⊤.justification: Affirmative state when a germanium atom achieves four geometrically precise covalent bonds.

⊥.justification: Negative state when an atom fails to achieve full tetrahedral coordination due to strain or impurity.

⊞.justification: The paradice where bonding and anti-bonding character coexist in the valence band structure.

⊡.justification: The high kinetic barrier permanently fixes the atomic positions into an append-only structural record.
